name: Akron
takeaway: Akron's Dynegy contract at 9.24¢ is approaching term end June 2026. Post-term rate unknown — contact accounts now before repricing locks in.
hook: Akron's city program with Dynegy is expiring in June — do you know what rate they're going to after that?
notes: Current supplier: Dynegy at 9.24¢/kWh. Term ends approximately June 2026. Ohio Edison territory. Verify exact term end date and new program rate. Note: Cuyahoga Falls and Wadsworth are municipal electric utilities — not eligible for competitive electric supply.

name: Green
takeaway: Green City shares Akron's Dynegy contract at 9.24¢ expiring June 2026. Active commercial corridor on SR-241 — outreach before repricing is the move.
hook: Green is on the same Dynegy contract as Akron — that term ends in June. Good time to see what options are out there.
notes: Green City, Summit County. Same Dynegy/Ohio Edison program as Akron. Term end approximately June 2026. Strong commercial/retail growth on SR-241.

name: Medina County
takeaway: Medina County has its own aggregation program at 9.50¢ through June 2028 — rate is confirmed and term is fresh. Stable now but worth tracking for the 2028 renewal.
hook: Medina County just locked in at 9.50¢ through 2028 — do you have accounts there that opted out of the county program?
notes: Medina County aggregation program (separate from NOPEC). Rate: 9.50¢/kWh, confirmed active May 2026 through June 2028. Ohio Edison territory. Accounts that opted out of the county program may be on a higher standard offer rate.

name: Stark County
takeaway: Stark County spans two utility territories: AEP Ohio (9.77¢) and Ohio Edison (9.34¢). Term ends August 2026 for both. Verify utility territory before pitching — rates differ by address.
hook: Stark County is split between AEP and Ohio Edison territories — do you know which utility your accounts there are on? Both programs are up for renewal in August.
notes: AEP Ohio territory: 9.77¢/kWh (Aug 2025–Aug 2026). Ohio Edison territory: 9.34¢/kWh (Aug 2025–Aug 2026). Both terms expire August 2026 — repricing exposure. Note: Beach City (Stark County) is a municipal utility — not eligible for competitive electric supply.

name: Kent / Portage County
takeaway: Kent and Portage County communities are in NOPEC territory. Rate jumps from 8.999¢ to 9.999¢ in June 2026 — same pain story as NE Ohio.
hook: Kent is on NOPEC — that rate is going up to 9.999¢ in June. Any of your Portage County accounts on the city program?
notes: Kent and surrounding Portage County communities are NOPEC members. Ohio Edison territory. Standard rate 8.999¢ rising to 9.999¢ June 2026. University/commercial mix in Kent proper.
